# The generated shapes — the chunk B1 sizing record

*This file records the word count of every shape the 1962 compiler generated in
the 90.05 object listing, and the evidence behind each count. One section per
family. It records what an analyst measured, and what grade of evidence stands
behind each number.*

The oracle is `test/fixtures/90.05-object-listing.target`, whose eighteen object
pages `test/fixtures/90.05-object-listing-notes.md` verified against the page
scans. `docs/design/m4-codegen.md` holds the decisions. This file holds the
measurements behind them.

## 1. What this file is, and what it is not

**It is a sizing catalogue.** A programmer implements chunk B1 from it. Chunk B1
matches the LOC column of the whole target, so every shape must carry the right
word count before any later chunk can match a printed line.

**It is not a design record and not a tutorial.** It states no decision, and it
does not explain the 709/7090 instructions or the MOVPAK protocol. Where a rule
needs a decision, the record that holds it is named. M4-8 holds the print rules.

**Section 6 is the point of the file.** It lists, in one place, every number the
compiler will emit that rests on one 1962 listing.

## 2. The method

### 2.1 Eight independent derivations from one artifact

Eight analysts each took one family. Each read the same artifact, a compact
rendering of the object listing, and derived its family alone. No analyst saw
another's result. The eight family names are used throughout this file:

| Family | What it sizes |
|---|---|
| structure | the program frame: DO, sections, END, STOP, GO TO, and the I/O calling sequences |
| descriptors | the pointer cells `SYS)132` and `SYS)133`, and the MOVPAK dispatch |
| figuratives | moves of BLANK, ZERO, HIGH.VALUE and LOW.VALUE |
| alphameric | the in-line alphameric moves, which take no MOVPAK dispatch |
| numeric | the numeric moves and the edited stores |
| arithmetic | SET, ADD, result storage and the truth function |
| compares | the comparisons, the skip vector, and the later-pass names |
| pool | the constant pool `CP)` |

Every count in this file was taken by octal subtraction of the LOC column,
twice.

### 2.2 The structural shapes were read twice

A second reader derived the structural shapes from the same artifact, without
sight of the structure derivation. This is the method the scan pass used on the
object pages: two readers who never met cannot hold the same wrong reading by
accident.

**The two readings agree on every shape, on every word count, and on the three
rules the sites carry**: a return cell is call-site-driven, a DO-addressed
paragraph returns where the next label starts, and a GET's resume label lands on
the first word after the AT END block. The one difference is coverage, not
content: the second reader's list of `FILE` sites omits LOC 01400 to 01402.

### 2.3 A ninth pass walked the eight derivations against the listing

The ninth pass walked all 42 statements of the procedure text against the
listing, in code. Section 3 holds the walk. It is the strongest evidence that
the catalogue is right, and it is what found the gaps.

### 2.4 What consumes a word

A generated line consumes one word of the location counter if, and only if, it
prints an octal word in the OCTAL column. Five line kinds consume **zero** words:
an `EQU`, a `USE n`, an `ORG`, a label-only line, and the instruction line under
an over-long label. Every LOC in this file is octal, as the listing prints it.

**An `EQU` line prints its equated value in the LOC column, not an address**, so
the column jumps out of order across it. The four in the procedure text print at
01741, 01405, 01742 and 01743, and each breaks a naive walk of the column.

**Never size a unit from the `+n` offset column.** That column counts printed
lines since the last line that carried a name, not words, and a label-only line
or an `EQU` line resets it.

**Two names on one word cost one word.** The first prints alone on its own line
and the second prints in the label column of the instruction, both at the same
LOC. Attested six times, at 00165, 00232, 00241, 00370, 01217 and 01472. LOC
00702 is a seventh label-only line and is not an instance: one name lands there,
and the interleaved `EQU` line pushes it up.

### 2.5 Three grades, used precisely

| Grade | Test |
|---|---|
| **derived** | a manual section grounds the rule, and the sample agrees |
| **pinned at the diff** | the print shows it, and no manual text derives it |
| **unrecovered** | no rule reproduces the attested values |

A fit is never a derivation. Where an analyst fitted a rule to the sites, this
file says so in the entry. Section 6 gathers all three grades, and each pinned
entry names the family whose derivation carries the label.

### 2.6 Operand conventions the counts depend on

- `PZE a,,d` prints the address first and the decrement second. Verified:
  `PZE CP)+26,,CP)+27` assembles `0 01727 0 01726`.
- `TXI a,t,d` with a zero decrement prints as `TXI a,t`.
- A `TXI` decrement prints in decimal, where the LOC column prints in octal. The
  fill of a 15-character field emits `,15`; read as octal that would be 13.
- `SYS)n` and `IOC)n` each assemble to absolute address `n`.
- `BL)n` and `PI)n` are one-based. `BL) BSS 3` at 01666 gives `BL)1` = 01666.
- A file name assembles to `04000 + k`, with `k` the one-based ordinal of the
  file's declaration in the ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
- Every I/O shape that carries a length carries the record's length in 36-bit
  words, never the file's BLOCKSIZE. ERRORFILE declares BLOCKSIZE 6 and its
  `IOST ERROROUT,,4` says 4, which is ERROROUT's own `BSS 4`.
- `RecordInfo.located` is true for a record that a file reads into a buffer.
  Such a record needs a base locator, and it prints in no `*DATA` storage map.
- `n)NAME` in the object listing is the *n*-th declaration of that name in
  DATA-division order, not a level number.

## 3. The statement walk, and what it found

### 3.1 The arithmetic of the walk

The procedure text runs from LOC 00165 to LOC 01620, with no break in the
column. Two independent counts give the same total: the span gives
0o1620 − 0o165 + 1 = 796, and the print gives 809 printed lines minus 13 that
consume no word — nine label-only lines, two over-long-label continuations and
four `EQU` lines.

**Every statement boundary lands.** The walk covers all 42 statements, 188 to
229. Each row was checked twice: the clause decomposition sums to the row's word
count, and each row's first LOC is the previous row's last LOC plus one. Both
checks pass on all 42 statements, and the column sums to 796.

**The eight derivations account for 781 of the 796 words.** 15 words fall inside
no shape that any derivation names. Section 3.3 lists every one.

**141 words are claimed by two families at once.** Summing the eight results as
written gives 922 words for a 796-word program. Section 3.4 assigns an owner.

Statement 187 generates zero words. It owns the label-only line `GN)000` at
00165, the same word as statement 188's `START TSX SYS)175,4`, so the walk's
lower boundary is measured and not assumed.

**One boundary was disputed, and the listing settled it.** The pool derivation
ended statement 202 at 00612; the compares derivation put statement 203's
compare at 00612 to 00616. The listing decides for compares: 00612 is
`CLA 3)HOURS` and 00613 is `CAS CP)+5`, the load and the compare of
`IF WORKING HOURS GT 40.0`, so statement 202 ends at its terminator, 00611.

### 3.3 The 15 words no derivation accounts for

**The alphameric MOVPAK movers, eight words, owned by no family.**

| LOC | Printed | Statement | Move |
|---|---|---|---|
| 00271, 00272 | `TXI SYS)240,1,21`, `TXI SYS)241,1,2` | 193 | MASTER `DAT` to ERROROUT `INFO`, `A(23)` |
| 00316, 00317 | `TXI SYS)240,1,15`, `TXI SYS)241,1,8` | 196 | DETAIL to ERROROUT `INFO`, `A(23)` |
| 01130 | `TXI SYS)239,1,15` | 208 | MASTER `NAME` to PAYRECORD `NAME`, both `A(15)` |
| 01137, 01140 | `TXI SYS)240,1,15`, `TXI SYS)241,1,3` | 208 | MASTER `NAME` to CHECK `NAME`, `A(18)` |
| 01353 | `TXI SYS)239,1,15` | 221 | MASTER `NAME` to BONDORDER `NAME`, `A(15)` |

Every family pushes these words elsewhere. The descriptors derivation sizes the
specific-move call at zero. The numeric derivation says the alphameric movers
belong to another family. The alphameric derivation names these exact sites and
says they are MOVPAK dispatches, not its own. The figuratives derivation covers
`SYS)243` to `SYS)245` only. No derivation gives the run a shape, a word count
or a selection rule.

**What the eight words show**, stated as an observation this file makes and not
as a rule any derivation carries: equal storage lengths on both sides take
`SYS)239` alone with the character count; a source shorter than its target takes
`SYS)240` with the source's character count, then `SYS)241` with the shortfall.
The arithmetic closes at all three two-word sites: 21 + 2 = 23, 15 + 8 = 23, and
15 + 3 = 18. **Three sites for the two-word form and two for the one-word form
is thin. Do not promote this to a derivation without saying so.**

**The THEN-arm join transfers, four words, described and never sized.** They are
`TRA GN)071` at 00545 (statement 200), `TRA GN)073` at 00636 (203), `TRA GN)075`
at 00671 (205) and `TRA GN)080` at 01312 (220). The compares derivation states
the rule exactly — a THEN arm that does not end in an unconditional transfer
gets one trailing `TRA <join>`, and a THEN arm that is itself a `GO TO` gets
none — and files it under layout words that are not part of the vector. No
formula includes them. The rule exists; the arithmetic does not.

**Three more, each an omission from a site list rather than a missing rule.**

| LOC | Printed | Statement | Why it is orphaned |
|---|---|---|---|
| 00546 | `TRA COMPUTE.PAY` | 200 | the one-word `GO TO` shape covers it, and both the site list and the tally of ten omit it |
| 01215, 01216 | `CLA CP)+10`, `STO 1)FICA,1` | 212 | `SET MASTER FICA = 144.00`. A one-term chain and a plain store compose to exactly these two words, and no site row covers them |

LOC 01215 and 01216 matter beyond the count. They are the program's only `SET`
whose right-hand side is a bare literal, so they are the one site that attests a
one-term chain: `CLA <pool word>` with no operand preparation.

### 3.4 The 141 words two families both claim

These are not disagreements about what the compiler emitted. They are
disagreements about which family owns the word. Every one makes a naive sum of
the eight results wrong.

| Families | Words | Where |
|---|---|---|
| descriptors and numeric | 84 | the 25 two-word `SYS)180` calls (50), and the pointer preambles plus `TSX SYS)182,4` at 00571, 00577, 01354, 01366, 01433, 01445, 01452 and 01464 (34) |
| descriptors and figuratives | 41 | the descriptor prologue plus `TSX SYS)182,4` at all thirteen figurative sites |
| arithmetic and compares | 16 | the three-word zero build at 00656–00660, the whole truth-function block at 01240–01252, and the base-locator guard at 01301–01302 |

**The first two are layering, not contradiction.** The descriptors derivation
sizes the specific mover at zero, and the numeric and figuratives derivations
size the whole unit. At every site the two agree word for word. **Rule for chunk
B1: the move family owns the whole unit, and the descriptor setup and dispatch
are a shared sub-shape counted once inside it.**

**The third is a real ownership dispute, and it points both ways.** The truth
function at LOC 01240 to 01252 is fully specified twice, at eleven words with
the same decomposition, so only the owner is in doubt. The zero build at 00656
is the arithmetic family's scale alignment and the compares family's three-word
load branch at once. The guard pairs at 01301 and 00661 are the arithmetic
family's base-locator prep and the compares family's operand prologue.

**A split that fits all three, offered as a proposal and not as a
measurement:** the comparison family owns every word from the first operand
preparation through the last vector slot, and the arithmetic family owns
everything else. The truth function then divides into a five-word frame — the
`RIR`, the `SIR`, the `PXA`, the `RFT` and the `CLA` of the true value — and a
six-word comparison unit. Five plus six is eleven, which is what both
derivations measured.

## 4. The shape catalogue

### 4.1 The program frame

| Shape | Trigger | Words | Attested sites, LOC (statement) |
|---|---|---|---|
| OPEN ALL FILES | the clause `OPEN ALL FILES` | 2 | 00165–00166 (188) |
| OPEN one file | `OPEN <file>` | 2 | none; [J 90.02.13] |
| CLOSE ALL FILES | the clause written in the source | 2 | 00517–00520 (199) |
| CLOSE one file | `CLOSE <file>` | 2 | none; [J 90.02.14] |
| STOP RUN | `STOP RUN` | 6 | 00521–00526 (199) |
| STOP n | `STOP <n>` | 3 | none; M4-14 and D2.7 |
| GO TO | an unconditional `GO TO` that is the whole clause | 1 | 00220 (189), 00307 (195), 00330 (196), 00341 (197), 00360 and 00367 (198), 00546 (200), 01164 (209), 01317 (220), 01416 and 01471 (225) |
| return cell | a procedure that at least one DO names | 1 | 00331 (197), 01165 (210), 01220 (214), 01262 (217), 01404 (224), 01473 (227) |
| terminal return | the end of a procedure that has a return cell | 1 | 00350, 01217 (213), 01261 (216), 01403 (223), 01472 (226), 01620 (229) |
| BEGIN SECTION | the clause | 0 | five sections |
| plain DO | `DO <p>`, no FOR and no TIMES | 3 | 00370–00372 (199), 00542–00544 (200), 00650–00652 and 00653–00655 (204), 00666–00670 (205) |
| DO FOR | `DO <p> FOR <i> = <p0>(<q>)<r>` | 11 + 5·M | 00702–00721 (206), M = 1, so 16 |
| statement stamp | one per GET | 1 | 00177 (188), 00221 (190), 00232 (191), 00276 (194) |
| THEN-arm join transfer | a THEN arm that does not end in a transfer | 1 | 00545 (200), 00636 (203), 00671 (205), 01312 (220) |
| base-locator initialization | always, in location counter 2 | 3 | 01666–01670 |

**The `GO TO` count is eleven sites, not ten.** The site list of the structure
derivation and its tally both omit `TRA COMPUTE.PAY` at 00546, the OTHERWISE arm
of statement 200. The shape covers it and the census did not.

**STOP RUN carries an implicit close-all.** Its six words are `TSX SYS)178,4`,
two `PZE CP)+a,,CP)+b` parameter words, the pair `TSX SYS)177,4 / PZE IOC)1`,
and `TXI IOC)40,0`, the end-of-job return point of the CT Monitor, [J 90.02.09].
No halt instruction is generated. Statement 199 therefore prints two `SYS)177`
pairs, its own `CLOSE ALL FILES` at 00517 and STOP RUN's close at 00524, and
M4-14 states the split.

**The statement stamp is one tag-0 `TXH CP)+a,0,CP)+b`.** Index register 0 does
not exist on the 7090, so the word is a no-op that carries two pool addresses.
STOP RUN carries its own pair as two `PZE` fields instead.

**`M` in the DO FOR count is the number of positional indicators the loop index
drives.** The prologue is 5 + 2·M words and the increment block is 6 + 3·M, and
the one site has M = 1.

**A return cell is call-site-driven.** END.OF.MASTERS is a plain paragraph and
carries a cell, because three `AT END DO` clauses name it. END.OF.DETAILS,
END.OF.RUN and NET carry none, because only a transfer reaches them.

### 4.2 Input and output

```
words(GET)  = 5 + (E > 0 ? 1 + E : 0)
words(FILE) = 3 + (located ? 2 : 0)
```

`E` is the size of the out-of-line AT END block. The extra word is the `TRA`
that jumps over that block, so it disappears with it.

| Shape | Trigger | Words | Attested sites, LOC (statement) |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET, `AT END DO` | E = 3 | 9 | 00177–00207 (188), 00221–00231 (190), 00276–00306 (194) |
| GET, `AT END GO TO` | E = 1 | 7 | 00232–00240 (191) |
| GET, no AT END clause | E = 0 | 5 | none; [J 90.02.29] |
| FILE, working-storage record | `RecordInfo.located` false | 3 | 00273–00275 (193), 00325–00327 (196), 00514–00516 (199), 01151–01153 and 01154–01156 (208), 01400–01402 (222), 01562–01564 (228) |
| FILE, located record | `RecordInfo.located` true | 5 | 01157–01163 (208) |

**The GET's five fixed words** are the statement stamp, `TSX IOC)8,4`,
`PZE <file>,,SYS)260`, `PZE <atEndBlock>,,SYS)283`, and the buffer descriptor
`IOCTN* BL)<n>,,<record words>`. With no AT END clause the fourth word takes
`SYS)265`, [J 90.02.29]. Each GET consumes two consecutive generated names, the
block first and the join second.

**The `AT END DO` block is the plain-DO triple, unchanged.** Its `AXT *+3,7`
names the join word, so the paragraph returns to the GET's resume point.
Verified: `AXT *+3,7` at 00205 assembles `0774 00 7 00210`, and 00210 is
`GN)059`.

**The located-record FILE adds `LXA BL)<n>,4` and `SXA GN)<a>,4`.** The pair
stores the run-time buffer address into the address field of the `IOST` word,
which carries the generated name.

**The descriptor mnemonic prints `IOCTN*`, where Appendix 90.02 prints
`IOCDN*`.** The attested octal supports the listing: the word assembles
`5 00017 6 01667`, and the 709/7090 channel-command encoding puts IOCD at prefix
0 and the IOCT family at prefix 5 *(external: 7090 channel command prefix
encoding)*. **M4-20 item (f) settled this on 2026-08-05.** The listing's fourth
glyph reads as a T at 40× magnification, each conversion is faithful to its own
source, and neither is an erratum. The compiler emits `IOCTN*`.

### 4.3 Descriptor setup and MOVPAK dispatch

This family fills the move source cell `SYS)132` and the move target cell
`SYS)133`, and enters MOVPAK. Its words are counted inside the move families,
under the ownership rule of section 3.4.

```
familyWords(S, T) = 2                            when the source is a register
                  = setup(T) + setup(S) + 1      otherwise
```

| Setup shape | Trigger | Words | Sequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| none | the mover does not read that cell | 0 | |
| fixed location | the operand's record is not located | 2 | `LDI CP)+nn / STI SYS)13x` |
| located record, simple locator | the record is located, and its locator always carries byte 0 | 3 | `CAL BL)n / ACL CP)+nn / SLW SYS)13x` |
| located record, complex locator | the operand follows a variable-length array | 6 | [J 90.02.11] case 3; no site |
| positional indicator | the operand is a subscripted reference that resolves to `PI)n` | 2 | `LDI PI)n / STI SYS)13x` |

| Dispatch entry | Words | Calling sequence |
|---|---|---|
| `SYS)179` | 3 | `TSX` plus a source address word plus a target address word |
| `SYS)180` | 2 | `TSX` plus a target address word |
| `SYS)181` | 2 | `TSX` plus a source address word |
| `SYS)182` | 1 | `TSX` alone; both cells are preset |

**The selection rule has two branches and no others.** The compiler emits
`SYS)180` when the source is a machine register, and `SYS)182` in every other
case. `SYS)179` and `SYS)181` are never generated. The rule is exercised 51
times with no counter-example.

**Which cells the move needs.** A cell is set in line if, and only if, the
specific-move subroutine that follows reads it. A figurative or in-line literal
source sets no source cell, because the value travels in the fill call.

| Group | Cells set in line | Sites | Setup and dispatch words |
|---|---|---|---|
| memory to memory | `SYS)133`, then `SYS)132` | 9 | 5 + 1 at 00263, 00310, 00577, 01122, 01131 and 01345; 4 + 1 at 01366, 01433 and 01452 |
| memory to register | `SYS)132` alone | 4 | 3 + 1 at 00571; 2 + 1 at 01354, 01445 and 01464 |
| figurative or literal source | `SYS)133` alone | 13 | 3 + 1 at 00342 and 00361; 2 + 1 at the other eleven |
| register to memory | none; the target rides in the `SYS)180` sequence | 25 | 0 + 2 at each |

The counting closes: 26 `SYS)182` dispatches, `SYS)133` set 22 times, `SYS)132`
set 13 times, and 22 + 13 − 26 = 9 two-cell sites. **The family costs 155 words
of the sample's 796**, 79 of in-line setup and 76 of dispatch.

**The 25 `SYS)180` sites**, at the `TSX`: 00374, 00402, 00410, 00416, 00426,
00434, 00442, 00450 and 00507 (199); 01071, 01077, 01105, 01115 and 01144 (208);
01274 (219); 01325 (221); 01475, 01503, 01511, 01517, 01525, 01533, 01541, 01547
and 01555 (228). All 25 carry a fixed-location target word `PZE LOC,,BYTE`.

**No reuse, ever.** Every dispatch re-emits, in line, every cell its mover
reads, with no liveness analysis and no reuse inside one statement. Three
witnesses: LOC 01131 repeats LOC 01124 word for word, seven words later in one
statement; LOC 01445 repeats the `PI)2` pair set at 01435; LOC 00547 repeats the
target setup of LOC 00167. **This rule most affects the word count, and a modern
implementer will get it wrong by optimising.**

**Target before source**, at all nine two-cell sites. The corner is untested:
every one of the nine has a two-word target block, so "target first" and
"cheaper block first" never diverge.

**The in-line address word is not drawn from the pool.** LOC 00442 emits
`PZE INS.PREM,,3` in line while `CP)+60` holds the same word.

**The guard rides on the index-register load alone.** `CAL BL)n` carries no
`TXL SYS)294` guard at any of its nine sites, and no formula in this catalogue
counts the guard twice.

### 4.4 Figurative-constant fills

A move of BLANK, ZERO, HIGH.VALUE or LOW.VALUE compiles to one unit per target.
A unit is a target-descriptor prologue, then `TSX SYS)182,4`, then a fill call.

```
words(unit) = D + 2 + F

D = 2, 3 or 6   the descriptor prologue of section 4.3, by where the target lives
F = 0           BLANK or ZERO; the fill call is one TXI
F = 1           HIGH.VALUE or LOW.VALUE; SYS)245 adds one in-line OCT word
```

| `D` | `F` | Words | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 0 | 4 | attested, eleven units |
| 3 | 1 | 6 | attested, two units |
| 2 | 1 | 5 | both forms grounded; the combination has no site |
| 3 | 0 | 5 | both forms grounded; the combination has no site |
| 6 | 0 or 1 | 8 or 9 | the complex locator itself has no site |

**The two axes are independent.** The prologue length follows where the target
lives, [J 90.02.11]; the fill length follows which subroutine fills it,
[J 90.02.25] and [J 90.02.26]. In the sample the only `SYS)245` sites are also the
only located targets, so the listing alone cannot separate the two. The manual
breaks the confound, and an implementer must not couple them.

**The unit size does not grow with the target's length**, so chunk B1 can size
every unit before any field length is known.

**Every site**, 13 units and 56 words: 00167–00172 and 00173–00176 (188, both
4); 00342–00347 (197, 6, located); 00361–00366 (198, 6, located); 00462–00465,
00466–00471, 00472–00475, 00476–00501 and 00502–00505 (199, all 4);
00547–00552 (201, 4); 00672–00675 and 00676–00701 (205, both 4); 01313–01316
(220, 4).

**A multi-target move emits one complete unit per target, in source order, with
no sharing.** Statement 199 shows all three parts: five targets inside one
record, five separate prologues against five separate pool cells, 20 words, in
the order NAME, EMPLOYEE, MONTH, DAY, YEAR.

**The fill count is the target's storage extent, not its digit count.**
`MOVE ZEROS TO INTERNAL.TOTALS` emits `TXI SYS)244,1,54` where the group's nine
pictorials sum to 57 digits. The storage map reserves nine words for the area,
`test/fixtures/90.05-storage-section.tsv` line 89, and 9 × 6 = 54.

### 4.5 In-line alphameric moves

The compiler moves an alphameric field to an alphameric field in line, with no
MOVPAK dispatch, when four conditions hold: both operands are alphameric; the
two storage lengths are equal; the source lies wholly inside one word; and the
target spans at most two words. Otherwise it emits the dispatch of section 4.3.

Terms: `L` is the character count, `sB` and `tB` are the source and target byte
positions inside their words, and `D` is `tB − sB`.

| Shape | Trigger | Words | Attested sites, LOC (statement) |
|---|---|---|---|
| whole-word move | `sB = 0`, `tB = 0`, `L` a multiple of 6 | 2·(L/6) | 00563–00570 (202, with two guard pairs), 01320–01323 (221, with one) |
| mask insert | `tB + L ≤ 6` and `D = 0` | 5 | 01006–01012 and 01026–01032 (208) |
| literal insert | the source is an alphameric literal, `tB + L ≤ 6` | 5 | 00256–00262 (193), 00320–00324 (196), 00455–00461 (199) |
| shifted mask insert | `tB + L ≤ 6`, `D ≠ 0`, `tB > 0`, `tB + L < 6` | 6 | 00210–00217 (189), 00553–00562 (201), 01013–01020, 01046–01053 and 01062–01067 (208) |
| accumulator shift chain | `tB = 0`, `L < 6`, `D ≠ 0`, `sB + L = 6` | 5 | 01021–01025 (208) |
| MQ shift chain | `tB > 0`, `tB + L = 6`, `D ≠ 0` | 6 | 01054–01061 (208) |
| two-word chain | `sB + L ≤ 6` and `6 < tB + L ≤ 12` | 11 | 00771–01005 (208, with a guard pair), 01033–01045 (208), 01332–01344 (221) |

**Add two words for each index-register load the statement forces.** The guard
pair is `LAC BL)n,i / TXL SYS)294,i,0`, once per load and never per reference.
The first two ranges above therefore print 8 words, and the first two-word chain
prints 13.

**The four single-word triggers partition the case with no overlap and no gap.**
The mask insert wins over both shift chains whenever `D = 0`. It needs one pool
word where the shifted mask insert needs two, because `COM` manufactures the
select mask from the clear mask. Every mask checks bit for bit against the
computed byte offsets.

**The literal insert is the mask insert with a pool cell for a source.** The
compiler materialises the literal with its characters already at the target's
byte offset and BCD blanks elsewhere, which makes `D = 0` by construction.

**The two-word chain is the strongest arithmetic result in this family.** Its
six shift distances are confirmed at three sites with three distinct
combinations of the byte positions, so they are derived and not fitted. The
chain emits `RQL 0` at two of the three, which is what keeps the count at 11.

**Statement 208 expands into nine per-pair blocks, and the two receivers
interleave.** The order is CHECK, then PAYRECORD five times, then CHECK three
times, although the source writes `MOVE CORRESPONDING DETAIL TO PAYRECORD,
CHECK`. This is not a misread of the symbol qualifiers: the byte geometry of
each block matches its assigned record independently, and only this assignment
fits. The interleaving belongs to the CORRESPONDING family, and no rule here
predicts it.

### 4.6 Numeric moves and edited stores

| Shape | Trigger | Words | Attested sites, LOC (statement) |
|---|---|---|---|
| edited store | the value is in the accumulator and the target is an edited field | load + divide + 5 | 25 sites, listed below |
| digit-split divide | `S.digitCount > T.digitCount` | 2 | 00424–00425 (199), 01113–01114 and 01142–01143 (208) |
| external decimal to register | source external decimal, target a register | preamble + 2 + store | 00571–00576 (202), 01445–01451 and 01464–01470 (225) |
| edited field to register | source an edited field, target a register | preamble + 1 + 3 + store | 01354–01362 (221) |
| external decimal to edited | | targetPre + sourcePre + 1 + 5 | 00577–00611 (202), 01433–01444 and 01452–01463 (225) |
| edited to edited | | targetPre + sourcePre + 1 + 5 | 01366–01377 (221) |
| internal decimal to internal decimal | equal scale, right justified, single precision | 2 | 01417–01420 (225) |

The pointer preamble is 2 words for working storage or a positional indicator,
3 for a simple base locator, 6 for a complex one, and 0 when the edited store
carries its target in the calling sequence.

**The edited store's five-word call is constant**: `TSX SYS)180,4`,
`PZE T,,byte`, `TXI SYS)267,1,editControl`, `OCT controlWord`, and
`AXT T.digitCount,1`.

**The 25 edited-store sites** are LOC 00373–00400, 00401–00406, 00407–00414,
00415–00422, 00423–00432, 00433–00440, 00441–00446, 00447–00454 and 00506–00513
(199); 01070–01075, 01076–01103, 01104–01111, 01112–01121 and 01141–01150 (208);
01273–01300 (219); 01324–01331 (221); 01474–01501, 01502–01507, 01510–01515,
01516–01523, 01524–01531, 01532–01537, 01540–01545, 01546–01553 and 01554–01561
(228). Three of the 25 carry the digit-split divide.

**Whole-block cross-checks.** Statement 199's CORRESPONDING expansion, LOC 00373
to 00432, is 32 words: five units of six, one of which carries the divide.
Statement 208's expansion is 26 words and statement 228's is 54, nine plain
units.

**The `AXT` counts the target's digit positions, and it is not a constant.** It
takes 5, 6 and 7 across the sites. LOC 00433 to 00440 separates it from the
control word's decrement: the control word holds 3 and the `AXT` holds 5,
because that target carries one fraction digit where every other carries two.

**The edit control prints in decimal and the manual states it in octal.** LOC
01146 prints `TXI SYS)267,1,12` and punches decrement octal `00014`, the
dollar-sign bit plus the decimal-point bit of [J 90.02.17] Note 1. That one site
separates the two readings.

**One site emits a real `TRA` where the others emit a `TXI`.** When the edit
control computes to zero, LOC 01327 punches `0020 00 0 00413`, opcode `TRA`,
where LOC 00376 punches a `TXI` to the same address. The count does not
change.

**The step-word count decides every run length.** Walk the target's digit
positions from the high-order end and emit one word per stretch that takes the
same treatment:

```
steps = (Ti > Si ? 1 : 0)      leading zeros to insert
      + (Si > Ti ? 2 : 0)      overflow test, then high-order bypass
      + 1                      the move, always present
      + (Tf > Sf ? 1 : 0)      trailing zeros to insert
      + (Sf > Tf ? 1 : 0)      low-order bypass

run   = 2 + steps + 1          an edited target: head, control word, terminator
run   = 1 + steps + 1          a register target: head and terminator, no OCT
```

`steps` is 2 at every edited-target site and 1 at the one register-target site.
Its floor is 1. **Every edited-target run in the sample is therefore five
words**, and the run never moves off five in this program. The one-word call to
`SYS)184` sits outside the formula, because [J 90.02.16] writes it as a complete
call.

### 4.7 SET, ADD and result storage

Notation: `S(x)` is the compile-time scale of `x` in powers of ten. For a data
item it is `ItemSemantics.fractionDigits`.

| Shape | Trigger | Words | Attested sites, LOC (statement) |
|---|---|---|---|
| additive chain | the top operator is `+` or `−` | 1 + (n − 1) + prep | 00625–00626 (203), 00722–00732 (207), 01207–01213 and 01215–01216 (212), 01227–01230 (215), 01307–01311 (220) |
| base-locator prep | the operand's record is located and the register is not live | 2 | 00637–00640 (203), 00661–00662 (205), 00727–00730 (207), 01175–01176 (211), 01222–01223 (215), 01263–01264 (218), 01301–01302 (220) |
| result-storage park | a chain operand that must be computed first | 1 | 00621 and 00624 (203), 01211 (212), 01226 (215), 01362 (221) |
| multiplicative step | a `*` node | 2, or 1 when the left value is already the MQ half | 00617–00620, 00622–00623, 00627–00630, 00641–00642 (203), 00656–00657 (205), 01166–01167 (211), 01221–01225, 01231–01232, 01241–01242, 01253–01254 (215) |
| scale alignment | an additive operand whose scale is below the chain scale | 3, or 4 when it chains onto a finished product | 00622–00624 (203), 00656–00660 (205), 01225 and 01241–01243 (215) |
| plain store | the expression scale equals the target scale | 1 | every chain above |
| scaling store tail | the expression scale exceeds the target scale | 5, or 4 under TRUNCATED | 00631–00635 and 00643–00647 (203), 01170–01174 (211), 01233–01237 (215) |
| non-binary operand fetch | the operand's class is not internal decimal | the convert of section 4.6, plus 1 to park | 01354–01362 (221) |
| ADD to a target | the `ADD` verb with a target list | per target: 3 + prep + tail | 01175–01201 (211), 01256–01260 (215), 01263–01272 (218), 01362–01365 (221) |
| ADD CORRESPONDING | the `ADD` verb with CORRESPONDING | per matched pair: 3 + prep + tail | 00733–00757 and 00760–00770 (208), 01565–01617 (228) |
| truth function | `TR(<relation>)` as an arithmetic factor | 1 + prep + 1 + V + 1 + 3 | 01240–01252 (215) |
| subscript-store update | a store into a subscript variable | 5 per positional indicator | 01421–01432 (225), two indicators |
| result-storage area | always, once per program | 0 words of text; `RS) BSS N` | 01621 |

**The equal-scale chain costs one word per operand after the first.** Statement
207's six-operand chain is the clean case: one `CLA`, five `SUB`, one guard pair
for the located operand, one `STO`, which is 9 words.

**A literal enters the pool as its keyed digits, never pre-multiplied by an
alignment factor.** The alignment is a run-time multiply against a separate pool
word: statement 203 multiplies the literal 20 by 100 rather than folding it to
2000. **This is the strongest structural fact in the family, and every site
obeys it.**

**An alignment inverts a comparison, and the inversion is load-bearing.** The
aligned value ends in the accumulator, so the literal becomes the accumulator
operand and the field becomes the storage operand. The skip vector then reads
greater, equal and less against the literal, and its arms mirror. Both attested
sites do this, statement 205 and statement 215's truth function. **A generator
that ignores it emits correct-looking code with inverted branches.**

**The store tail is `XCA / ACL half / LRS 35 / DVP scale / STQ target`.** The
half-adjust word is present by default and `TRUNCATED` suppresses it. The
divisor is shared with any alignment multiply of the same power, and the
half-adjust constant gets its own pool word: 500 with 1000, and 50 with 100.

**A result-storage cell is two words**, so the address of cell `m` in section `k`
is `base(k) + 2m`, which D4.8 records. The five referenced cells give section
bases 0, 6, 10 and 16. `RS) BSS 30` at 01621 and `TS) BSS 7` at 01657 are 30
words apart, so the section blocks are packed with no gap.

**The truth function is eleven words at its one site**, and its frame is five:
the `RIR`, the `SIR`, the `PXA`, the `RFT` and the `CLA` of the true value.

### 4.8 Comparisons and the skip vector

`CAS` and `LAS` each leave control at one of three fixed one-word slots, at
compare + 1, + 2 and + 3, for greater, equal and less. The order is the
documented order of the three return words of the out-of-line comparison
subroutine, [J 90.02.12], and the in-line vector reproduces it.

```
V = 3 − (the less continuation is the next word to be emitted ? 1 : 0)
```

**Only slot 3 can be dropped, and that is a derivation, not a habit.** The slots
sit at fixed displacements from the compare. Dropping slot 2 would put the
following code at compare + 2, and the less outcome would then land one word
inside that code.

| Shape | Trigger | Words | Attested sites, LOC (statement) |
|---|---|---|---|
| numeric compare | both operands numeric, each holding in one word | P(A) + L(A) + P(B) + 1 + V | 00612–00616 (203), 00656–00665 (205), 01202–01206 (212), 01241–01246 (215), 01301–01306 (220), 01405–01415 (225) |
| alphameric compare | both operands alphameric, or a logical compare | P + 1 + E + spill + P + 1 + E + V | 00241–00250 and 00251–00255 (192), 00332–00340 (197), 00351–00357 (198), 00527–00541 (200) |
| out-of-line compare | a field the compiler cannot compare in one word | 9 | none; [J 90.02.12] |

`P(x)` is the index-register prologue, 2 words when the operand's record is
located and the register does not already hold that base, and 0 otherwise.
`L(A)` is 1 for a plain load and 3 for a zero operand that must be built and
scaled. `E(x)` is the extraction cost of an alphameric sub-word field, one word
for `LGL` when the field does not start at byte 0 and one for `ANA` when it is
shorter than six characters. When both operands need extraction, the first is
spilled to a result-storage cell for one more word.

**All eleven attested vectors obey the count**, six on `CAS` and five on `LAS`.
Five drop a slot and six do not. A two-slot elision is a legal encoding and is
not attested; do not implement it.

**Each emitted slot prints a symbol when the generator holds one for that
outcome, and the relative form otherwise.** It holds a symbol for a target the
source named and for an arm or join label the front end allocated, and none for
the THEN arm, the next `WHEN` clause's compare, the fall-through past the last
clause, or the interior of a truth function.

**A false outcome goes to the OTHERWISE arm's own label, not to the join.**
Attested three ways, at statements 203, 205 and 225, where each OTHERWISE arm
carries its own label and a separate join label follows.

**The index-register cache is real and must be modelled.** The sample reuses a
register inside a straight run, and reloads at LOC 00555, 01301 and 01405. **The
accumulator is never cached**: LOC 00251 re-issues a load for a value the
accumulator already holds. Section 6.4 holds the two incompatible rules that
explain the three reloads.

### 4.9 The later-pass generated names

The front end allocates `GN)000` to `GN)083` in source order. The code pass
continues from `GN)084`. Six of the ten names 084 to 093 are bound and print:
`GN)085` as `EQU SEARCH+1` at 01405, `GN)086` on the increment block at 00711
and `GN)088` as `EQU CP)+37` at 01741, all in statement 206; `GN)089` on the
patched `IOST` word at 01163, statement 208; `GN)091` as `EQU CP)+38` at 01742
and `GN)093` as `EQU CP)+39` at 01743, both in statement 225.

**The pass walks the emitted text in ascending object address**, and the three
machinery sites at 00702, 01157 and 01421 take ascending runs. This is firm.

**The four unprinted names were never bound, not suppressed.** The listing prints
two names on one word as two lines whenever both exist, six times over, so the
printer has no rule that hides a redundant name. [J 90.02.02] states the same
behaviour. A name on a fall-through word would still have printed.

**Two groupings reproduce the print, and the listing cannot separate them.**
M4-6 as amended carries the first. Both are fitted.

| Site | First grouping | Second grouping |
|---|---|---|
| DO FOR, statement 206 | 084 to 088, binding 085, 086 and 088 | the same |
| FILE of a buffered record, statement 208 | 089 and 090, binding 089 | 089 alone |
| the RETPREM subscript, statement 225 | 091 and 092, binding 091 | 090 and 091, binding 091 |
| the INSPREM subscript, statement 225 | 093 and 094, binding 093 | 092 and 093, binding 093 |

Nothing in the sample decides between them, because the counter ends at 093 and
094 is unobservable.

## 5. The constant pool

### 5.1 Four sub-pools, filled independently

The pool holds 62 entries at LOC 01674 to 01771, one word each. It is four
sub-pools, filled independently and concatenated in one fixed order at layout
time:

| Sub-pool | Indices | Count | What it holds | Order within |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| literals | 0–13 | 14 | the values written in the PROCEDURE source, plus one subscript stride | source order, after two seeds |
| machine words | 14–36 | 23 | masks, BCD statement stamps, BCD verb text, the figurative fill, scale and round constants | first need |
| subscript bases | 37–39 | 3 | `PZE symbol±offset`, no decrement | first need |
| descriptors | 40–61 | 22 | `PZE symbol,,byte` | first need |

**The pool is not in first-need order as a whole.** The first generated
statement, 188, references `CP)+40`, `CP)+14` and `CP)+15`, and never `CP)+0`.

**Each of the last three sub-pools is in first-need order.** Read in emission
order, the first reference to each entry falls in strictly ascending index order
inside each of them. Merging any two destroys the ordering, because entries 40
and 41 are needed before entries 14 and 15, so the segregation is real and is
not an artifact of this program's shape.

**The literal sub-pool is in source order, and two inversions prove it.** First,
statement 215 writes `0.18` before `13`, so they take indices 11 and 12, while
the generated code loads index 12 before index 11. Second, the stride at index
13 is first emitted at 00714, three words ahead of the literal 12 at index 8.

**Two entries precede every source literal.** Index 0 holds the integer 0 and
index 1 the integer 1. Source order alone would place them at indices 6 and 7.
These are the two entries that rest on the print alone.

**Indices are assigned in a layout pass, not during generation.**
`GN)088 EQU CP)+37` is emitted at statement 206, when the machine-word sub-pool
still held 21 of its 23 entries, so the index 14 + 23 was not computable then. A
generator must emit a reference as a sub-pool and a key, and resolve every
`CP)+NN` after generation ends.

**`ZEROS` and `BLANKS` produce no pool entry**; they compile to fill calls.
`HIGH.VALUE` does produce a word, in the machine-word sub-pool.

### 5.2 The keying rule

> Two constants collapse into one entry exactly when they land in the same
> sub-pool and their keys are equal. The key of an `OCT` entry is its 36-bit
> word value. The key of a `PZE` entry is its printed symbolic operand — the
> qualifier, the name, and the offset or decrement — never the assembled bits.

Four attested discriminators:

1. **An `OCT` entry keys on the word, not on the source text.** Statement 205
   writes `ZERO` and statement 215 writes `0`. One entry, `CP)+0`, referenced at
   00656 and 01241.
2. **An `OCT` entry merges across statements.** `CP)+31` serves statements 203,
   205, 211 and 215, at seven sites.
3. **A `PZE` entry does not merge on bits.** `CP)+38` and `CP)+39` both assemble
   `0 00000 0 00134`, and they are two entries.
4. **A `PZE` entry does not merge on bits, harder.** Entries 43 to 46 all
   assemble `0 00000 0 00000`, and they are four entries, because their operands
   are four different names.

**A useful negative.** `1)DAT` and `1)EMPLOYEE.NUMBER` are the same displacement
in the same record and stay separate, because the compiler wrote two names.

**The pool dedupes across every move family.** `CP)+40` serves statements 188
and 201. `CP)+55` serves statements 205 and 220 and a non-figurative move at
LOC 01366. `CP)+47` serves statement 199 and a non-figurative move at LOC 01122.

**The flag column follows the address.** It prints `10000` for every `OCT` entry
and for every `PZE` entry whose address field is a pure displacement, and
`10001` for every `PZE` entry whose address field is a program location. The
correlation is exact over all 25 `PZE` entries: the six displacement words carry
`10000` and the other nineteen carry `10001`.

## 6. What is ours

This section lists every rule a generator will follow that the manuals do not
state. A reader must be able to find, in one place, every number the compiler
will emit that rests on one 1962 listing.

### 6.1 Derived — a manual section grounds it

1. The GET calling sequence's four words after the stamp, and `SYS)265` in word
   4 when no AT END clause is written. [J 90.02.04], [J 90.02.29].
2. OPEN and CLOSE, two words each, for one file and for all files.
   [J 90.02.13], [J 90.02.14].
3. STOP RUN's `SYS)178` call, its two BCD parameter words, and `IOC)40` as the
   end-of-job return point. [J 90.02.14], [J 90.02.09].
4. The three in-line descriptor setups and their counts, 2, 3 and 6 words.
   [J 90.02.11] cases 1 to 3.
5. The four MOVPAK dispatch entries and their counts, 3, 2, 2 and 1 word.
   [J 90.02.14], [J 90.02.15].
6. The three address-word forms, `PZE LOC,,BYTE`, `MZE BL)nn,,CP)+nn` and
   `MON PI)nn,,0`. [J 90.02.14], [J 90.02.15].
7. The base-locator guard pair `LAC BL)n,i / TXL SYS)294,i,0`, two words per
   register load. [J 90.02.23], [J 90.02.04].
8. The three fill subroutines, and the second word that `SYS)245` alone carries.
   [J 90.02.25], [J 90.02.26].
9. The step vocabulary, the meaning of each step's decrement, the mapping from
   family to step, and the terminator as the target numeric length.
   [J 90.02.16] to [J 90.02.19], [J 90.02.30].
10. `SYS)184` is a complete one-word call, with no control word and no
    terminator. [J 90.02.16].
11. The head decrement 1 on the edited-field-to-register call. [J 90.02.30].
12. The edit-control bit set, and the four fields of the target control word.
    [J 90.02.17] Notes 1 and 2.
13. The `AXT` carries the number of digits to convert, in its address field.
    [J 90.02.30], separated from the control word's decrement at LOC 00433–00440.
14. Family selection by the source and target field classes. [J 90.02.15] to
    [J 90.02.19], [J 90.02.30].
15. The comparison slot order, greater then equal then less. [J 90.02.12].
16. Only slot 3 of a skip vector can be dropped. The slots sit at fixed
    displacements from the compare, so dropping an earlier slot moves the later
    outcome inside the following code.
17. The nine-word out-of-line comparison calling sequence. [J 90.02.12].
18. The pool sits after the positional indicators, and every attested entry is
    one word. [J 90.02.06].
19. The result-storage total is the sum over sections of the maximum each
    section uses. [J 90.02.03]. The per-section maximum is item 3 of section 6.3.
20. The three unattested fill words of the collating table: LOW.VALUE in the
    native sequence, and both values under `COLLATE COM`. [J 02.04.02] fixes the
    glyph and the repository's BCD table, D0.6, fixes its code. Section 6.4
    records a disagreement about this entry.
21. The printer prints each name of a word on its own line. [J 90.02.02].
22. The alphameric fill count is the target's storage extent, not the sum of its
    pictorial digits. Two independent witnesses, the emitted 54 and the storage
    map's nine-word reservation. The figuratives derivation grades this a
    derivation on the second witness; no manual section states it.

### 6.2 Pinned at the diff — the print shows it and nothing derives it

40 rules across the eight derivations have the listing, and nothing else, as
their authority. Each entry names the family that carries the label. A rule the
family labelled unattested or manual-only is not in this list, because that is a
gap in evidence rather than a claim made on the listing's authority.

**descriptors**

1. The positional-indicator setter `LDI PI)n / STI SYS)13x`. [J 90.02.11] gives
   three cases and this is a fourth. Four sites.
2. The dispatch selection rule: `SYS)180` when the source is a register,
   `SYS)182` otherwise, and never `SYS)179` or `SYS)181`. The manual permits the
   two cheaper entries at thirteen sites, and the compiler pays 29 extra words
   to decline them.
3. No reuse, ever: every dispatch re-emits every cell its mover reads. Three
   witnesses, no counter-example, no manual text.
4. Target cell before source cell. Nine sites agree, but none pairs a located
   target with any source setup, so "cheaper block first" survives.

**figuratives**

5. One unit per target of a multi-target move.
6. Units emitted in source order.
7. No sharing of a descriptor, a `TSX` or a pool constant between two targets of
   one statement, even inside one record.
8. Constant-pool dedup by target descriptor across all move families, with
   first-use allocation order.

**alphameric**

9. The whole in-line and MOVPAK boundary: both operands alphameric, equal
   storage lengths, source inside one word, target inside two. A generalisation
   of the listing; [J 90.02] says nothing about in-line move shapes.
10. The selection rule for the accumulator shift chain, inferred from one site.
11. The selection rule for the MQ shift chain, inferred from one site.
12. The selection of the eleven-word two-word chain. Its arithmetic is derived
    from three sites; its selection is pinned.
13. The field-source form of the mask insert. This is an addition to M4-9,
    attested twice and stated nowhere.
14. The receiver interleaving of `MOVE CORRESPONDING DETAIL TO PAYRECORD,
    CHECK`: CHECK, then PAYRECORD five times, then CHECK three times. The
    alphameric derivation declines to derive it.

**numeric**

15. `TRA SYS)267,0,0` replaces the `TXI` when the edit control computes to 0.
    One site, confirmed by the punched opcode.
16. `LDI PI)n / STI SYS)132` as a pointer preamble. Four sites; [J 90.02.15]
    gives a positional indicator a different form.
17. The target pointer is set before the source pointer. Four sites of four, no
    text.
18. The terminator decrement of the edited-field-to-register call is the
    source's digit count. One site, where two readings coincide.

**arithmetic**

19. The per-section result-storage maximum. Sections 0, 1 and 2 reserve 3, 2 and
    3 cells while referencing 2, 1 and 1. No tested rule fits all three.
20. `ADD CORRESPONDING` target order, reversed at its one site, where the one
    plain `ADD` site goes the other way.
21. The result-storage cell number, the count of chain operands that follow the
    operand in source order. Four sites, one discriminating.
22. `RS)1+0` printed at LOC 00621 against the bare form everywhere else. A
    printed form with no rule behind it, scan-verified.
23. Base-locator register liveness. See section 6.4.

**compares**

24. A figurative constant goes into the accumulator in an equality compare. Two
    sites, one construct.
25. The index-register liveness cache, which is the second and incompatible
    formulation of item 23.
26. The truth-function block, which works only because the true outcome is the
    less outcome. One site, and the operand placement there was forced.
27. The run lengths that reproduce the generated names `GN)084` to `GN)093`.
    **Fitted, not derived**: three sites cannot determine four run lengths, and
    the placement of `GN)090` and `GN)092` is undecidable from this listing.
28. The negative rule that a two-slot elision is legal and unattested. Do not
    implement it.

**structure**

29. Tag 7 on the plain DO's `AXT` against tag 4 on the DO FOR patch's.
30. `PZE <file>,,0`, the zero decrement of the FILE call.
31. The sub-statement number. **Fitted**, to two informative sites, with the
    competing comma-count rule rejected only by a page-scan reading. See
    section 6.4.
32. The `EQU` line placement rule, and the use of a generated name rather than a
    direct `CP)+n` reference for the three positional-indicator pointers.
33. `TRA SEARCH+1` and `TPL GN)085` naming one address two ways in one block.
34. The GET join label's three printing placements.
35. One base locator per located record, shared across an input file and an
    output file, numbered from `BL)2`. Two sites.
36. Section numbers 4 and 5 for SEARCH and DEPARTMENT.END, inferred from
    ordering alone.

**pool**

37. The seeded head: indices 0 and 1 hold the integers 0 and 1 ahead of every
    source literal.
38. The boundary between the literal sub-pool and the machine-word sub-pool. The
    table stride sits with the literals while the scale factors sit with the
    machine words. One entry carries the rule.
39. The concatenation order of the four sub-pools. Each sub-pool's internal
    order is evidenced; the order between them is only the printed layout.
40. The GET statement stamp itself. [J 90.02.04]'s READ sequence carries no
    `TXH CP)+a,0,CP)+b` word.

**One observation, outside the 40, made by this file and by no derivation.** The
selection between the one-word and the two-word alphameric mover run of section
3.3 rests on five sites and nothing else. It is thinner than any item above.

### 6.3 Unrecovered — no rule reproduces the attested values

1. **The clause digits of the statement stamp's second word.** See section 6.4.
2. **The `TS)` block size.** The sample reserves seven words and the program
   addresses none of them, so no demand-driven rule can return 7. M4-4 as
   amended takes the attested 7 as a constant, on Jack's call, and forbids any
   fitted rule. For any program but the sample, our size is unverifiable.
3. **The per-section result-storage maximum.** Sections 0, 1 and 2 reserve 3, 2
   and 3 cells while referencing 2, 1 and 1. "Highest index plus one spare"
   fails section 2 by one cell. "Operands in the largest chain" and "non-leaf
   nodes in the largest statement" both fail statement 207, whose six-operand
   chain needs no cell at all. Sections 3, 4 and 5 share the remaining seven
   cells in an unknown split.
4. **The printed form `RS)1+0`.** Emit the offset suffix at LOC 00621 and the
   bare form everywhere else. No rule accounts for it.
5. **The roles of the two unbound names inside the DO FOR run.** The positions
   of `GN)084` and `GN)087` are certain and their meanings are not. Any
   five-name template whose second, third and fifth members are the body entry,
   the increment block and the table base fits the print equally.

Items 1, 3 and 4 also appear in section 6.2, because a derivation labelled each
of them pinned at the diff: item 1 as the structure derivation's sub-statement
number, items 3 and 4 as the arithmetic derivation's. They carry the stronger
warning here. A pinned rule reproduces the sample and rests on the print alone,
and these three reproduce the sample only by naming the sites.

### 6.4 Five questions the derivations do not answer the same way

**Question 1, the clause digits of the statement stamp.** The second stamp word
holds the character the listing prints as a comma, then two digits, then three
blanks. The attested digits are `02` for statement 188, `00` for statements 190,
191 and 194, and `14` for statement 199.

- *The pool derivation reports the rule unrecovered.* Counting comma-separated
  clauses gives `03` for statement 188, where `02` is attested, and `14` for
  statement 199, which is attested. Counting one clause per verb gives `02` for
  statement 188, which is attested, and `10` for statement 199, where `14` is
  attested. No tested rule reproduces both non-zero values. Its instruction is
  to specify the two words as a pair, take the digits from whatever the clause
  counter yields, and diff.
- *The structure derivation offers a fitted rule and labels it pinned at the
  diff.* The digits are the zero-based ordinal of the clause within its
  statement, where each target of a multi-target MOVE counts as its own clause
  and `OPEN ALL FILES` is not counted. That reproduces all five sites. It also
  rejects the comma-counting rival on evidence: the rival needs statement 188 to
  carry no comma after `INTERNAL.TOTALS`, and the page scan
  `comtran-manuals/J28-6169/images/page-195.png` shows the comma. The structure
  derivation states its own residual: the rule needs `OPEN ALL FILES` excluded
  and `CLOSE ALL FILES` included, the listing offers no second instance of
  either, and two data points constrain a rule with three free parameters.

The ninth pass sides with the pool derivation, and gives its reason: this is the
`TS) BSS 7` situation, and a fitted rule would be worse than an honest gap. Both
derivations agree that a generator can reproduce the sample from the table in
section 5.3 alone. **Settled by ruling — the addendum below.**

*Addendum, 2026-08-15, chunk B1.* Jack ruled for the fitted rule: M4-14 as
amended holds the zero-based clause ordinal, with its two one-site counting
exceptions stated as such. The ninth pass's recommendation did not stand.

**Question 2, base-locator register liveness.** Both derivations label their
rule pinned at the diff, and the two rules are not the same. The arithmetic
derivation says the compiler reloads at a label, at a section entry, and after
any MOVPAK calling sequence, and reuses the register inside a straight run. The
compares derivation says the compiler caches what index registers 1 and 2 hold,
and clears the cache at any word that carries a label and at any instruction
that writes the register. They explain the same three reload sites, 00555, 01301
and 01405, by different mechanisms: at 01301 the compares reading is that the
`AXT 6,1` at 01300 wrote the register, and the arithmetic reading is that a
MOVPAK sequence intervened. No site separates them, because every MOVPAK
sequence in the program ends in an `AXT` that writes index register 1. A
generator must pick one, and the pick is unforced. **Settled at the diff — the
addendum below.**

*Addendum, 2026-08-15, chunk B1.* Two sites this entry did not weigh separate
the readings, and neither reading survives whole. Statement 203 reuses
MASTER's register at 00627 across both MOVPAK sequences of statement 202, so
a full post-MOVPAK reload contradicts the listing — the guard at 00637 is the
OTHERWISE label's clear. And statement 221 reuses the register at 01332
across the edit tail at 01331, inside its CORRESPONDING expansion, where
statement 220 reloads at 01301 across statement 219's identical tail. The
register-write kill therefore holds at statement distance and defers inside
an expansion; M4-9 as amended carries the composite the oracle confirmed.

**Question 3, who owns the truth function, the zero build and the guard pair.**
Section 3.4 holds both claims and a proposed split. The word counts agree; only
the owner is open.

**Question 4, the internal-decimal move.** The numeric derivation specifies it,
two words at LOC 01417 to 01420, and then recommends that the arithmetic family
own it. The arithmetic derivation never picks it up, and its site tables hold no
row for those two words. The shape is specified by a derivation that disclaims
it. **Chunk B1 must count it once.**

**Question 5, the grade of the HIGH.VALUE fill word.** Both derivations agree on
the emitted word, `OCT 747474747474` at LOC 01723. The pool derivation grades it
from the diff, because [J 90.02.09] names the four figurative-constant classes and
gives no word for any of them, so the sample is the only witness. The
figuratives derivation grades it derived, and says so explicitly: [J 02.04.02]
fixes the glyph, the repository's BCD table, D0.6, fixes that glyph's code, and
the three unattested cells of the same table follow by the same route. The
disagreement changes no emitted word. It changes whether a reader may trust
those three fill words, which section 6.1 item 20 carries. **The question is
open.**

## 7. What no site exercises

A later reader must not mistake silence for coverage. Nothing below has an
attested shape in this listing.

**Verbs and clauses with no site.** `OPEN <file>` and `CLOSE <file>`; a GET with
no AT END clause; `STOP <n>`; `DO ... EXACTLY n TIMES`; a multi-index DO; the
USING and GIVING parameter forms; `GO TO (p1,…,pn) ON <index>`.

**Shapes the manual describes and the program never uses.** The complex base
locator, six words, in every family that could carry it; no `PDX` and no
`TXL *2` appears anywhere in the listing. The `MZE` and `MON` target forms of
the `SYS)180` calling sequence. The dispatch entries `SYS)179` and `SYS)181`.
The specific movers `SYS)183`, `SYS)186`, `SYS)187`, `SYS)188` and `SYS)189`.
The out-of-line comparison, and with it the boundary that would select it.

**Steps and controls with no site.** The trailing-zero step, both bypass steps,
the overflow test, the sign scan, and the round step. The leading-zero step is
never omitted, because every site has more target integer digits than source
integer digits. The control word's prefix field, since every target pictorial is
comma-free, and its tag field, since every site prints sign convention 0. The
edit-control bits for the asterisk, the comma and blank-when-zero; only the
decimal point and the dollar sign are exercised.

**Data shapes with no site.** An alphameric literal longer than six characters,
so `ceil(chars / 6)` is a guess, and an alphameric literal whose target does not
start at byte 0. A subscripted or repeated target of a figurative move, which
[J 02.04.02] permits. A group with an interior alignment gap. A source that
straddles two words in an in-line move, a multi-word in-line move, and an
indexed target in every in-line shape but the whole-word move. A pictorial that
carries an `S` filler, which would separate the digit count from the stored
digit positions. A numeric source over ten digits. A located target in an edited
store; all 25 sites reach a statically-addressed target.

**Figurative cells with no site.** LOW.VALUE anywhere. BLANK into internal
decimal or floating point, where the chart stores zeros. BLANK into external
decimal. ZEROS into an edited or scientific-decimal target. The sample exercises
two of the chart's twenty-four cells, BLANK into alphameric and BLANK into
edited, plus two group targets the chart does not cover at all. Every other
cell's choice of subroutine is read off the chart text and D4.11.

**Options and limits with no site.** `TRUNCATED`, which D4.1(b) rules
suppresses the half-adjust word and nothing else. `ON ERROR` in an environment
description, so what replaces `SYS)283` is unknown. `ON OVERFLOW`. Division,
exponentiation, double precision and mode promotion. A downscale of a value in
the accumulator, since every attested store tail follows a multiply. A store
tail on an `ADD` or an `ADD CORRESPONDING` pair, since every attested pair has
equal scale. The 500-entry pool ceiling behind message 172, D9.7; this program
uses 62. Whether the pool can be empty.

**Two facts about sections have no witness.** Section numbers 4 and 5, for
SEARCH and DEPARTMENT.END, are inferred from the ordering of the `BEGIN SECTION`
clauses, and neither uses result storage. And all five sections are named by a
DO, so the listing cannot say whether declaring a section alone earns a return
cell. Do not claim that it does or that it does not.
